facts.text: I have really bad pain in my right arm.
It started three days ago.

facts.item: arm pain: what you were doing when it started
facts.text: I was playing with my grandchildren in the garden when I tripped and fell.
I stumbled over a toy on the floor and tried to brace myself with my right arm, but I ended up landing on my hand.
I didn't lose consciousness.
It's in the upper and middle parts of my right arm.

facts.item: arm pain: at the moment of the fall
facts.text: I didn't feel any pain when I first fell.

facts.item: arm pain: how it came on
facts.text: Then the pain started gradually.

facts.item: arm pain: change since it started
facts.text: It is stable now, but it is still there.
I used a sling and took Tylenol, but the pain only improved slightly.

facts.item: arm pain: using an ice pack
facts.text: I also used an ice pack at home.

facts.item: arm pain: what makes it better
facts.text: Not moving my arm and taking Tylenol make it better.

facts.item: arm pain: what makes it worse
facts.text: Using my arm makes it worse.

facts.item: arm pain: seeing a doctor for it
facts.text: I haven't seen a doctor since the fall.

facts.item: arm pain: why you didn't come in sooner
facts.text: It wasn't that bad, and I thought it would get better on its own. Also, I didn't want to bother my son. He doesn't have time to bring me to the hospital. He is busy.
My arm isn't weak.
I believe I can move it in all directions, but it hurts when I do.
My arm isn't numb.

facts.item: loss of feeling in the arm
facts.text: I can feel things fine.
I don't have pain anywhere else.
I have asthma.
They removed part of my prostate 2 years ago.
They said there was no evidence of cancer.
It was very difficult for me to urinate, but that has since gotten much better.
I am allergic to aspirin.
I get an itchy rash all over my body.
I take Tylenol.
I use an albuterol inhaler.
I don't work anymore. I am a retired schoolteacher.
I do not drink alcohol.
I don't smoke.
I walk 20 minutes every day to the grocery store and back.
I live with my son in his house.

facts.item: living situation: who else is at home
facts.text: My son is married and has three kids.
Life has been hard on my son lately. He lost his job and is looking for a new one.
I feel safe.

facts.item: being hurt or threatened at home
facts.text: Nobody bothers me.
They are all nice.

findings.name: head examination
findings.result: Normal head shape; no signs of trauma; no bruises.

findings.name: neck examination
findings.result: Supple; full range of motion in all directions; no bruises.

findings.name: lung auscultation
findings.result: Breath sounds clear on both sides.

findings.name: heart examination
findings.result: Regular rate and rhythm; normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs or gallops.

findings.name: right arm and shoulder examination
findings.result: He holds the right arm close against the chest wall with his left hand, externally rotated and slightly abducted. Non-localized tenderness over the middle and upper right arm and the right shoulder. Pain when the right shoulder is moved in any direction, with restricted range of motion in flexion, extension, abduction and external rotation. Right elbow and wrist normal.

findings.name: motor strength
findings.result: Unable to assess because of pain.

findings.name: sensation
findings.result: Intact to pinprick and soft touch.

findings.name: reflexes
findings.result: Deep tendon reflexes intact and symmetric.

findings.name: arm pulses
findings.result: Brachial and radial pulses normal and symmetric.

other_considerations.note: Red flags in the history (anxious behavior, delayed care-seeking) may point to it; abuser and victim often both deny abuse, so the diagnosis is often inferential and supporting evidence must be sought.
Usually nonspecific shoulder pain often referred down the proximal lateral arm, with possible inability to abduct or flex the shoulder and weakness in internal or external rotation.

source_issues: p014 (parser merge): the question field holds the patient's answer to 'Reason for Not Seeking Medical Attention' ("...when it wasn't that bad, and I thought it would get better on its own? Also, I didn't want to bother my son. He doesn't have time to bring me to the hospital. He is busy."), followed by the 'Living Conditions' question. In the raw sheet the answer is written on the Doctor line and the doctor's actual question is missing. The answer field is the Living Conditions answer. Annotated from the correct content (f015, f033-f035), keeping id p014.

p015 (parser merge): the question field joins the 'Social History' question ('Is there anyone else living with you? Do you have a significant other?'), which has no answer in the raw sheet, with the 'Safety/Elder Abuse Screening' question; the answer belongs to the safety question. Whether he has a significant other is unknown.
Note HPI says he used 'Tylenol and an ice pack at home'; the script (p011) says a sling and Tylenol. The ice pack is added as a flagged note-only fact (f011).
Note HPI says he 'fell on his outstretched right arm'; the script says he braced with 'my arm' and landed on his hand without naming the side.

Note PMH lists 'BPH' and PSH 'Prostatectomy'; the patient says only that part of his prostate was removed 2 years ago for difficulty urinating with no evidence of cancer. BPH is a clinician interpretation and was not copied into patient facts.
Note SH: 'Walks for 20 minutes every morning'; script says every day.
Gold diagnosis #1 'pain increases with hand movement': the script describes pain with using or moving the arm, not the hand. Its exam line is one comma-separated sentence, split into three items.
Gold diagnosis #2 exam finding 'Right arm externally rotated and slightly abducted' comes only from the SP notes; the note exam says only 'Right arm held closely against chest wall'.

p006: the patient believes he can move the arm in all directions, while the SP is told not to allow full shoulder range of motion and the note exam records restricted ROM; recorded as the patient's belief.
The sample closure ends with a stray page-number artifact '(203 206)'.
notes: The home-safety denials (f036, f037) are coded absent and flagged because the script has him look anxious while giving them; the stage direction is kept in acting_notes.

f010 (sling and Tylenol give only slight relief) and f012 (not moving the arm and Tylenol make it better) come from different questions and are both kept; f027 records Tylenol as a current medication.
Prostate history: surgery is historical; the voiding difficulty is historical and 'much better', not explicitly resolved.
The lack of insurance appears only in the challenging question and is kept in patient_questions.

'Sit up in bed' is positioning only and is not an exam finding; the arm position, pain on shoulder movement and restricted ROM (v1 x020-x022) are merged with the note's arm findings into the arm and shoulder record x010.

Conversion: the two reasons for the delay (v1 f019, hpi, and f020, social) answer one scripted question and are one child fact (f015) so that the question gets the whole answer; living with the son (p014) is f033 with the son's family as a child, and the son's job loss is a stressor (f035).

Conversion: the fall details (p003) are a separate fact (f004) next to the context child f003; the aspirin reaction (p018) is a child of the allergy (f026); 'no evidence of cancer' is a child of the prostate surgery (f023).

Conversion: 'Appears anxious' is in the general-appearance record (x005) because the note's exam records it; otherwise it would stay a behavior. The note's 'VS: Within normal limits' (e002) agrees with the doorway values and is cited on all four doorway records.
